description:
FILED s457aj (Opus agent AJ, round 14), the measured residue of #820.

#820 made the ALL-CAPS bareword-handle convention UNICODE:
`Pl::Environment::all_caps_shape` is `\p{Lu}[\p{Lu}\p{Nd}_]*`, so `áº ` (U+1EA0,
Lu) is handle-shaped exactly as `BEE` is.  A CASELESS script has no uppercase
letter, so it still fails the test.

REPRO (probed 5.40.3; the shape is perl's OWN t/uni/readline.t:31,
`open á, '.' and binmode á and sysread á, $_, 1`):

    use utf8;
    open á, '<', $f or die;      # U+157D CANADIAN SYLLABICS, category Lo
    my $c = <á>;
    print "1:", (defined $c ? $c : "UNDEF\n");
    # perl: L1        PCL: UNDEF     (base AND post-#820 -- unmoved)

SILENT, and only in a NON-STRICT file: under `use strict` the word is
classified a CALL and `%p-fh-arg`'s macro-time rescue of a `(pl-NAME)` form
recovers the handle, which is why t/uni/readline.t (strict from line 29) does
not move.  `FÊ` (U+029C LATIN LETTER SMALL CAPITAL H, category Ll -- also in
that file) is the same gap from the other side.

THE OPEN QUESTION, and why #820 stopped short: the candidate widening is
"starts with a letter and contains no \p{Ll}", which admits a caseless script
AND keeps the ASCII inverse only if the leading `_` is still excluded
(File::Path's `_IS_MSWIN32` is named in handle_subcalls' comment as
deliberately slipping the ALL-CAPS escape).  It is a CLASSIFIER widening, so
it owes the gate-SET scan over both populations plus the four-population
emission A/B -- #820's recipe, which found exactly the intended files.

NOTE the deliberate split #820 left behind: `all_caps_shape` (Unicode) answers
the HANDLE/TERM/indirect-object questions, `all_caps_call_guess` (ASCII) the
"keep an unplaceable bareword a CALL" question in handle_subcalls, because
THERE a wrong yes turns a value perl prints into an undefined-subroutine
death -- measured, it cost `no strict; print "x=", áº¸;`.  Any widening here
must keep that split or re-measure it.
subject: A bareword filehandle in a CASELESS script (`open ᕽ, '<', $f`) is still silently wrong in a non-strict file -- #820's residue
